title: Strategic Considerations for Assessing Alignment of ASEAN and Asia Pacific Countries with Security and Economic Blocs Dominated by Major Powers
what_it_is: Strategic Considerations for Assessing Alignment of ASEAN and Asia Pacific Countries with Security and Economic Blocs Dominated by Major Powers

sections.label: Quad, AUKUS, IPEF, BRICS expansion
sections.summary: The emergence of the Quad, AUKUS, IPEF and BRICS expansion are part of a response to a transition from a unipolar to a multipolar world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: More recently, we have also seen the emergence of the Quad, AUKUS and the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework (IPEF) and of course, even more recently, the expansion of BRICS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: These recent developments, in fact, are part of a response to a transition from a unipolar world to a multipolar world.

sections.label: Joining groupings and national interests
sections.summary: Decisions on whether to join a specific grouping must be carefully considered and clearly defined by Singapore's national interests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Ultimately, our decision on whether or not to join a specific grouping must be carefully considered and must be clearly defined by our national interests.

sections.label: Singapore does not take sides
sections.summary: Singapore does not take sides but will uphold principles, even if it must sometimes say no to close partners or superpowers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Singapore does not take sides; but we will uphold principles, even if this means, from time to time, having to say "no" to other states, some of which can be our close partners or even superpowers.

sections.label: New arrangements and ASEAN centrality
sections.summary: New emerging arrangements must not undermine ASEAN centrality and should support an open, inclusive, rules-based regional architecture based on international law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: What is important for Singapore is that these new emerging arrangements, especially where they intersect with our region, do not undermine ASEAN centrality, and that these arrangements support an open and inclusive regional architecture and promote a rules-based order based on international law.

sections.label: Engaging everyone, not taking sides
sections.summary: Singapore does best when it can engage everyone, not by taking sides or being a vassal or proxy state, which would invite proxy wars.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I would submit that in fact, this is the most sensible position for Singapore, a multiracial, multi-religious, multilingual city-state and an island in the heart of Southeast Asia, in which all the superpowers, and indeed, middle powers, have a stake.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And because of our geography, because of our economic role, we do best when we can engage everyone; not by aiming to take sides or be a vassal state or be a proxy state, which in fact, I think it will be a recipe for disaster and invite the recreation of Southeast Asia as an arena for proxy wars.

sections.label: Domestic consensus and defence spending
sections.summary: Domestic politics must stop at the water's edge, as it has for 59 years, and Singapore continues National Service and significant defence spending because no one would rescue it in a conflict.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And all the more so, because in fact, all the major civilisations and religions are represented here.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, I am making the point that there needs to be domestic consensus and our domestic politics must stop at the water's edge, that we have been able to do so for 59 years, and the point I am making is that we must continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: If we were ever to get into a security or military conflict, no one is going to rescue us.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: That is why we continue to have National Service.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: That is why we continue to spend a significant proportion of our budget on defence.
